I farm 57 mu, that is a lot of land for our village. I grow mostly maize because it feeds the family and the pigs, and the rest I put in stevia because the company comes to buy the dry leaves and pays cash. This year I will put 45 mu in maize and 12 mu in stevia, same as last year — no reason to change what worked.

For the maize, I do like I always do. Before planting I spread the compound fertilizer, the three-fifteen kind (15-15-15), two bags per mu. One bag is 50 jin, so that is 100 jin per mu before the plough goes in. Then when the maize is knee-high, I put urea, one and a half bags per mu down the row and cover it with soil before I water. My neighbor Old Wang does the same and his corn always stands tall. If I put less my leaves turn yellow and I lose grain — better to spend the extra fifty yuan on fertilizer than lose two hundred jin of grain.

I buy the hybrid seed from the shop in town, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever they have. The old seeds my father used do not yield anymore, everyone uses the new seed now. I plough with the tractor service — 40 yuan per mu — because rotary alone does not break the hardpan after the stevia roots.

I water the maize from the well. Three times usually — once after planting if no rain, once at tasseling which is the most important, and once when the grain is filling. The well pump uses electricity so I do not waste water.

For pests, I spray when I see the borer moths. Usually two sprays — one for the seedling cutworm and one for the borer in mid-summer. If there is armyworm I spray again, but usually two is enough.

For stevia, it is different. Stevia needs more care, the leaves must be clean and green or the company pays less. I put three bags of compound per mu before planting the seedlings, and I top-dress urea twice, one bag each time after each cutting. Stevia likes water, so I irrigate five, six times. Stevia gets aphids and leaf spot, I spray three or four times through the season. I use rotary tillage on stevia land because the seedlings are small and I do not want to turn up clods.

Last year my maize did about 1300 jin per mu (650 kg) and stevia dry leaf about 500 jin per mu (250 kg). I expect about the same this year if the weather holds.
